classic_bugs/INFO: Localizable.strings (en:77,214,253,267,286,287,346,348,350 and matching pt-BR/es keys) still use %d for Swift Int (64-bit) arguments, e.g. notif_discreet_body_fmt fed Int(saturating: threshold) at NotificationService.swift:158. This is the same class as BUG-MAE-014. Values are small today, but the fix is a sweep to %ld across the three languages, optionally with a validate.sh lint for %d in the strings files.

quality/INFO: NotificationService now threads the four values (vendor, label, threshold, token) through send -> deliveryFinished -> tracker.delivered/park/unmark (NotificationService.swift:124,150,184). Passing a single Crossing/PendingRef value would shrink these signatures and stop a future field from being dropped on one path. This is not introduced debt worth blocking this minimal fix.

title: notif_discreet_body_fmt still uses %d for a 64-bit Int argument (sibling of BUG-MAE-014)
evidence: content.body = L10n.localizedString("notif_discreet_body_fmt", Int(saturating: threshold)) against "crossed %d%%" in en.lproj:77 (and the same in pt-BR/es). threshold comes from the user-controlled notifications.notify_at [Double] (AppConfig.swift:167), which has no upper clamp, so a value above Int32 prints truncated, the same way BUG-MAE-014 did.
fix: Use %ld in all three Localizable.strings and extend NotificationTitleLocalizationTests to cover this key

title: Other %d format keys may receive Swift Int arguments
evidence: The keys service_status_ax_value_fmt, service_status_duration_fmt, reset_confirm_message, credits_local_msgs_fmt, credits_cloud_msgs_fmt and compare_vs_prev_*_fmt use %d. Check whether their callers pass Int (64-bit). If they do, switch to %ld in all three locales.
fix: Audit the callers and use %ld where the argument is Int

Same class as BUG-MAE-014, outside this batch: notif_discreet_body_fmt still uses %d for Int(saturating: threshold) in en/pt-BR/es (Localizable.strings:77/76/76; call site NotificationService.swift:158). It is harmless while thresholds stay within 32-bit range, and the correct specifier is %ld.
